issues.legal_issue: Agricultural land in the villages fell within the constitutional meaning of an estate even though the local landholding system did not establish an equivalent land-tenure estate.
material_facts: The properties were village holdings in a territory where land was dealt with by grants of permanent or period leases or by sale, rather than under a law of land tenures.
Payments to the government were rent or a percentage of presumable income from land, not land revenue under a land-tenure system.
The bulk of the village land was devoted to agriculture or pasture, and some was used for horticulture or purposes ancillary to agriculture.
issues.conclusion: The holdings did not qualify as estates by equivalence to the local land-tenure law and were not held under ryotwari settlement. However, land held or let for agriculture or ancillary purposes fell within the constitutional definition of an estate, so its acquisition or extinguishment was protected to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-A(2)(a) defines an estate by reference to local land-tenure law and also includes the specified grants, ryotwari land, and land held or let for agriculture or ancillary purposes. An estate in the ordinary Indian revenue-law sense requires land paying land revenue and held under a law relating to land tenures. The Court considered Sri Ram Narain Medhi v. State of Bombay, Mahadeo Paikaji Kolhe v. State of Bombay, Atma Ram v. State of Punjab, K. K. Kochuni v. State of Madras, P. Vajravelu Mudaliar v. Special Deputy Collector, N. B. Jeejeebhoy v. Assistant Collector, and Ranjit Singh v. State of Punjab.

predicates.agrarian_reform_proceeding: The case concerns a measure abolishing village proprietorship as part of agrarian reform.
predicates.local_land_tenure_system_absent: The land was held through leases or purchase, without a local law of land tenures or a land-revenue tenure system.
predicates.land_held_or_let_for_agriculture_or_anci: The land was held or let for agriculture or a purpose ancillary to agriculture.

issues.definition: When an agrarian-reform measure affects land held or let for agriculture or an ancillary purpose in a system without a local land-tenure equivalent, that land falls within the constitutional estate definition.

issues.legal_issue: A regulation defining covered land more broadly than the constitutional definition could operate within the constitutional boundary because its excessive reach was severable.
material_facts: The regulation defined land to include every class or category of land.
The constitutional definition of estate, as retrospectively amended after the regulation was made, covered a narrower range of land.
The Court found that the regulation’s broad definition could be severed without preventing the regulation from operating on land within the constitutional definition.
issues.conclusion: The Court would not read the regulation’s definition down to match the constitutional definition, because the regulation predated the retrospective amendment. The definition was severable, and the regulation continued to operate, with constitutional protection confined to land within the constitutional definition of an estate.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-A(1) protects qualifying acquisition, extinguishment, or modification from challenges under Articles 14, 19, and 31; Article 31-A(2)(a) defines the relevant estate. The Court applied the severability principles in R. M. D. Chamarbaugwalla v. Union of India, distinguishing Romesh Thapar v. State of Madras and referring to State of Bombay v. F. N. Balsara. It also considered In re Hindu Women's Rights to Property Act and Punjab Province v. Daulat Singh on construing general statutory language within legislative power. The Court noted The Superintendent, Central Prison, Fatehgarh v. Ram Manohar Lohia without expressing an opinion on the competing approaches discussed there.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_land_aboliti: A party brought a constitutional challenge to a measure abolishing landholding rights.
predicates.measure_defines_covered_land_broadly: The measure describes the land affected more broadly than the land eligible for constitutional protection.
predicates.constitutional_protection_has_narrower_s: The constitutional protection covers a narrower class of land than the measure describes.
predicates.excess_scope_is_severable: The measure can continue to operate on the land within the protected class without the broader definition.

issues.definition: If a challenged land-abolition measure reaches beyond the protected class but that excess can be severed, the measure operates only within the protected class.

issues.legal_issue: Salt lands and pans, hills, quarries, and land within a municipal area were not brought within the constitutional agrarian-reform protection merely because the regulation included every category of land.
material_facts: Some village land consisted of salt lands and salt pans, hills, and quarries.
Part of one village lay within a municipal area containing houses, markets, and a cemetery.
Those categories were included by the regulation’s broad definition of land, but did not fall within the constitutional definition applicable to the agrarian land at issue.
issues.conclusion: The listed non-agricultural categories were not protected by Article 31-A. The municipal area did not vest in the government under the regulation; the other excluded categories were outside the regulation’s protected operation, and any acquisition of them required compensation assessed on other considerations.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-A(2)(a)(iii) covers land held or let for agriculture or ancillary purposes, including the specified waste, forest, pasture, and occupied-building lands. Article 31-A does not protect expropriation of land outside its definition of an estate. The Court applied the severability principle in R. M. D. Chamarbaugwalla v. Union of India to limit the operation and protection of the regulation to qualifying land.

predicates.land_abolition_proceeding: The case concerns a measure abolishing village proprietorship and vesting land in the government.
predicates.land_is_salt_hill_quarry_or_municipal: The land consists of salt land or pans, hills, quarries, or land within a municipal area.
predicates.land_outside_agricultural_estate_class: The land is not within the class of land held or let for agriculture or an ancillary purpose covered by the constitutional definition.

issues.definition: When a land-abolition proceeding concerns one of the specified categories outside the agricultural-estate class, that land does not vest under the measure.
